A new study finds younger and lower-income women
who are diagnosed with breast cancer
tend to see delays in care.
And Piersuki Noguchi has more.
Women under age 40 are not typically screened for breast cancer

if they have the disease because of their youth.
In a study published in the journal Cancer,
investigators looked at data to identify the wait time for care
among 1,000 individuals diagnosed with breast cancer
enrolled in the young women's breast cancer study.
It found 153 instances of patients,
particularly those who are lower-income,
facing delays of three months or more
to see a clinician about their symptoms.
Younger patients were likely to see treatment
delayed by two months or more.
The report says the delays may not have led

Yuki Noguchi, NPR News.

The thieves fled, leaving two paintings behind,

The theft has museums around France
